title: Practice 2: Rain falls, time flies, luck comes: the idioms

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Это судно ___ (везти — to convey by vehicle, one way) хлопок-сырец.
exercises.why: **везёт** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **везти** (to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **возить** for many directions. present: я везу́ · ты везёшь · он везёт · мы везём · вы везёте · они везу́т. — Wiktionary, «везти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **везти**: to convey, to carry (by vehicle), to deliver, to transport; (impersonal) to be lucky, to have luck, to work out for, to succeed, to be successful [with dative ‘for someone’ and infinitive ‘to do something’].  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «везти — Ей везёт / повезло. — She is lucky/got lucky.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note also the following idiomatic construction: Мне не везёт. — I am not lucky. Ему везёт. — He is lucky. Вам повезло. — You were lucky.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: The ship is carrying raw cotton.
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Том ___ (вести — to lead, take along, one way) себя как детсадовец.
exercises.why: **ведёт** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **вести** (to lead, to preside over, to chair) — the one-direction verb of its pair, with **водить** for many directions. present: я веду́ · ты ведёшь · он ведёт · мы ведём · вы ведёте · они веду́т. — Wiktionary, «вести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **вести**: to lead, to preside over, to chair; to drive; to keep.  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «вести — Страна ведёт войну. — The country is waging a war. · Девочка ведёт дневник. — The girl keeps a diary. · Дорога ведёт в город. — The road leads to the city. · Ложь к добру не ведёт. — No good comes from lying.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «This verb also follows the pattern of "going verbs". Note the following meanings: 1. to lead, to take: Я веду моего сына в школу. Я каждый день вожу его в школу. 2. to drive: Кто ведёт эту машину? Он не умеет водить машину. 3. to conduct: Противник ведёт огонь. 4. to behave oneself: Этот мальчик плохо ведёт себя. Note that in the last two examples (3 and 4) only the actual function verb "вести" can be used. (Never "водить").» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Обычно Том ___ (носить — to carry on foot, there and back or in general) очки.
exercises.why: **носит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **носить** (to carry, to bear (a burden)) — the many-directions (or there-and-back) verb of its pair, with **нести** for one direction. present: я ношу́ · ты но́сишь · он но́сит · мы но́сим · вы но́сите · они но́сят. — Wiktionary, «носить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **носить**: to carry, to bear (a burden); (of wind, water, etc.) to carry along, to drive; to have something (e.g. a name, sideburns, a gun...); to wear (clothes, shoes or makeup).  «The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. See below for examples.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «носить — Иван Иванович носит имя отца. — Ivan Ivanovich bears the name of his father. · Она носит красивую одежду. — She wears pretty clothing.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Note some special uses of these verbs: нести ответственность — to bear responsibility; нести потери — to suffer casualties; носить костюм (пальто, шляпу, ботинки etc.) — to wear (habitually); носить очки — to wear glasses.» — DLI, Lesson 78.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The uni- and multidirectional distinction rarely figures into the metaphorical and idiomatic use of motion verbs, because such phrases typically call for one or the other verb. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
